reference.source: Manson's Tropical Diseases; CDC parasitic disease guidance
clinicalPearls: A zoonotic tissue nematode infection acquired by eating raw or undercooked meat containing Trichinella larvae, classically pork but also wild game such as bear and boar
The early intestinal phase causes diarrhoea, abdominal pain and nausea within days of ingestion
The later muscle-invasion phase produces fever, myalgia, weakness and the characteristic periorbital and facial oedema
Marked peripheral eosinophilia and raised muscle enzymes (creatine kinase) are typical laboratory findings
Splinter haemorrhages, conjunctival and subungual haemorrhages, and a rash may be seen
Serology becomes positive over the first weeks; muscle biopsy showing encysted larvae is diagnostic when needed
Treatment combines anthelmintics such as albendazole or mebendazole with corticosteroids to control the inflammatory reaction in severe disease
Serious complications include myocarditis, encephalitis and respiratory muscle involvement, which are the main causes of death
reference.pathophysiology: Trichinellosis begins when a person eats raw or undercooked meat containing encysted Trichinella larvae. Gastric digestion frees the larvae, which mature into adult worms in the small intestine; the females release newborn larvae that penetrate the mucosa and disseminate through the bloodstream and lymphatics. These larvae preferentially invade striated skeletal muscle, where they encyst within modified muscle cells (nurse cells), provoking an intense eosinophilic and inflammatory response. This muscle invasion accounts for the myositis, myalgia and periorbital oedema, while migration through other tissues can inflame the myocardium, central nervous system and respiratory muscles, explaining the potentially fatal complications.
additionalDifferentials: Other causes of eosinophilia with myalgia (eosinophilia-myalgia syndrome, hypereosinophilic syndrome)
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count and blood film for eosinophilia
Serum creatine kinase and other muscle enzymes
Detailed dietary history for raw or undercooked pork or game
Muscle biopsy for encysted larvae in uncertain cases
ECG and cardiac assessment, and neurological evaluation, when complications are suspected
redFlags: Chest pain, arrhythmia or heart failure suggesting myocarditis
Headache, confusion or focal deficits suggesting encephalitis
Severe systemic illness with very high eosinophilia and muscle enzyme elevation
reference.prognosis: Most cases are mild and self-limiting with a good outcome, but heavy infections with myocardial, neurological or respiratory involvement can be life-threatening; prompt treatment shortens illness and reduces complications.
pitfalls: Missing the dietary history of undercooked pork or wild game
Mistaking the myositis and periorbital oedema for dermatomyositis or an allergic reaction
Relying on early serology, which may be negative in the first days of illness
Failing to give anthelmintics early, before larvae encyst in muscle, when the diagnosis is suspected
Overlooking cardiac or neurological complications that determine prognosis
management: Start a benzimidazole anthelmintic (albendazole or mebendazole) promptly to kill intestinal adult worms and curtail release of newborn larvae; efficacy is greatest early before muscle encystment

Add systemic corticosteroids for severe inflammatory disease, particularly myocarditis, central nervous system involvement or marked myositis, to suppress the intense eosinophilic hypersensitivity response
Provide supportive symptomatic care with antipyretics and simple analgesia for fever and myalgia, together with bed rest and adequate hydration
Institute early ECG and cardiac monitoring and watch for myocardial, neurological and respiratory-muscle complications, tracking eosinophilia and creatine kinase
Escalate to critical care for myocarditis with arrhythmia or heart failure, encephalitis or respiratory-muscle weakness
Refer to infectious diseases or tropical medicine, involving cardiology and neurology when organ involvement is suspected
Notify public health, trace the implicated meat source and advise thorough cooking or freezing of pork and game to prevent further cases and treat co-exposed individuals
